div.p: Miss C. K. Cumming informs Leonard Woolf that she had declined Woolf's job offer as the Hogarth Press manager in hopes of a better position being offered from other firms, and now regrets the decision. She asks Woolf that, since he has connections in the publishing industry, if he could inform her of opportunities in any firms expanding their business, as her application would have a higher rate of success. Typescript letter signed by C. K. Cumming.

You
Each first sentence of a new paragraph is indented to the right may think it rather extraordinary
that I should ask you for any help
See correspondences dating from 1928-01-20 and 1928-01-24 in archive folder 'SxMs-13/1/Q/3/D: Correspondence with and about employees and prospective employees'. The first letter was from Leonard Woolf to invite Miss C.K. Cumming to come work for him as Press Manager. The second letter is Miss C.K. Cumming's response to Mr. Woolf's letter, in which she declines his offer., but things have
come out very unhappily for me.
I think that the thing that really
weighed most with me in January
See letters from 1928-01-20 and 1928-01-24. and caused all my vacil-
lation and consequent wrong decision was the fact that
I had previously had some dealings with another firm.
I felt then that if an offer came to me from that firm,
I might want to accept it, and that I ought not to
accept your post with that possibility in my mind. I
can't think now why I ever thought I might prefer it
and I have regretted a hundred times both my indecision
and my over-scrupulousness.
Anyhow, after keeping me in suspense for
weeks (it is months since the first conversation), they
have finally decided to promote someone inside the firm
instead (just what I might have expected) and the whole
thing falls to the ground, a great disappointment.
This means that I have to begin again to
canvass all the firms in London, which is very disheart-
ening. It is so difficult to know the right moment.
What I thought I would ask you is this.
As you are inside the publishing world, you might pos-
sibly hear in advance that some firm was contemplating
changes or expansion. An application under those cir-
cumstances would stand a much better chance of receiving
attention. If you ever did hear of such a thing and
would let me know, I should be immensly grateful, and
would not use your name at all, if you did not wish it.
I hope you will not think that I am taking too great a
liberty in asking you.

closer.salute:
Yours sincerely
Indented to the right in original letter, albeit further than the first sentence of each paragraph.
